verdict.rationale: Better Auth documents a built-in rate limiter with stricter default rules for sign-in paths (`/sign-in/email` limited to 3 requests per 10 seconds) and configurable IP-header tracking, which directly addresses brute force; a community user corroborates that rate limiting is built in. Bot detection and IP blocking appear only as a one-line homepage claim, and nothing specifically addresses credential stuffing. missing for 10: documented bot-detection/CAPTCHA mechanism, credential-stuffing defenses (e.g. breached-password checks or account lockout), detailed docs on IP blocking, independent hands-on corroboration beyond rate limiting.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can rely on built-in protection against bots, credential stuffing, and brute-force attacks on the auth flows

citations.quote: Better Auth includes a built-in rate limiter to help manage traffic and prevent abuse.
`/sign-in/email`: Is limited to 3 requests within 10 seconds.
Security & observability. Bot detection, IP blocking, and email validation.
things like email verification, password resets, and rate limiting come built-in or as simple plugins
